{{Short description|UK and Canada bowling and minigolf centre operator}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2018}} {{Use British English|date=December 2018}} {{Infobox company | name = Hollywood Bowl Group PLC | logo = Hollywood_Bowl_Group_logo.png | image = Hollywood Bowl Score Screen.jpg | image_alt = The image shows what a score screen looks like at one of Hollywood Bowl's locations | image_caption = An example of the score screen at Hollywood Bowl in Yeovil | type = [[Public company|Public]] | traded_as = {{lse|BOWL}} | industry = [[Entertainment]] | founded = {{Start date and age |1960}} | founder = US company [[AMF Bowling]] | hq_location_city = [[Hemel Hempstead]] | hq_location_country = [[United Kingdom]] | key_people = Darren Shapland ([[Chairman]])
Stephen Burns ([[CEO]]) | products = Bowling alleys, minigolf sites | revenue = {{increase}} [[Pound sterling|£]]250.7 million (2025){{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodbowlgroup.com/application/files/5417/6769/7101/HollywoodBowl_AR25_Full_report.pdf|title=Annual Results 2025|publisher=Hollywood Bowl Group|access-date=28 January 2026}} | operating_income = {{decrease}} [[Pound sterling|£]]59.4 million (2025) | net_income = {{increase}} [[Pound sterling|£]]34.6 million (2025) | num_employees = | website = {{URL |hollywoodbowlgroup.com}} }} '''Hollywood Bowl Group''' is a British company that runs the ''Hollywood Bowl'' branded multi lane [[ten-pin bowling]] and ''Puttstars'' brand [[minigolf]] centres in the UK, and ''Splitsville Bowl'' branded ten-pin centres in Canada (with three centres also offering [[five-pin bowling]], as of April 2026). It is listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] and is a constituent of the [[FTSE 250 Index]]. == History == === Foundation as AMF Bowling UK === The United States company [[AMF Bowling]] opened its first centre in the United Kingdom in [[Stamford Hill]], North London on 20 January 1960. Between 1967 and 1970, AMF Bowling UK acquired its first 15 centres. After [[Goldman Sachs]] purchased AMF Bowling in 1996, the number of centres owned and operated by AMF Bowling in the UK rose in 1997 from 15 to 37. The company then embarked on a program to refurbish the acquired centres.{{cite web|url=http://www.globalretailjobs.com/company/1724/The-Original-Bowling-Company|title=Company Info: The Original Bowling Company|accessdate=9 February 2014}} In 2004 certain shareholders of the British leisure conglomerate, [[Bourne Leisure]], acquired the AMF-branded centres in the UK. AMF Bowling UK then embarked on another programme of refurbishment and since 2007 had opened five new centres in the UK. === The Original Bowling Company === In August 2010, AMF Bowling UK acquired the Hollywood Bowl business from [[Mitchells & Butlers|Mitchells & Butlers PLC]] and combined the companies into The Original Bowling Company Ltd (TOBC), UK’s largest bowling centre operator. TOBC sold centres to 1st Bowl (now known as MFA Bowl) as part of the merger.{{cite web|url=http://talktenpin.net/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=8813&Itemid=139|title=About The Original Bowling Company Limited|accessdate=8 February 2014}} In September 2014, [[Electra Private Equity]] acquired TOBC for £91 million.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidermedia.com/insider/midlands/122870-ten-pin-bowling-giant-bought-91m/|title=Ten Pin Bowling Group Bought for £91M|date=8 September 2014|website=Insider Media Ltd.}} In 2015, TOBC purchased rival Bowlplex.{{cite web|url=http://leisureopportunities.co.uk/detail.cfm?pagetype=detail&subject=news&codeID=319831|title=The Original Bowling Company takeover of Bowlplex wins CMA approval|date=7 December 2015|website=Leisure Opportunities}} TOBC itself then rebranded as Hollywood Bowl Group (HBG). After purchase of Bowlplex, the company phased out the Bowlplex and AMF branded centres and rebranded them (as the already its biggest brand of its three) Hollywood Bowl.{{cite web|url=http://www.bowlersjournal.com/?p=10362|title=U.K.'s Bowlplex Chain to Be Acquired by TOBC|date=22 April 2015|website=[[Bowlers Journal]]}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.cityam.com/original-bowling-company-strikes-take-over-bowlplex/|title=The Original Bowling Company strikes to take over Bowlplex|date=22 April 2015}} ===The pandemic and new ventures=== On 15 August 2020, the company, along with other bowling centres and casinos, reopened all its centres after over four and a half months of not being able to operate. Two planned Puttstars opened for the first time as their original opening dates were pushed back due to lockdown. Rules to protect staff and customers were put in place to keep people inside of the centres from contracting [[COVID-19]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-53450410|title=Coronavirus: How will bowling alleys and casinos change after lockdown?|date=29 July 2020|website=[[BBC News]]}} In 2022, the company bought the Canadian Splitsville brand to expand out of the UK, with further openings and acquisitions to expand the Splitsville brand.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/business/hollywood-bowl-buys-canadian-brands-in-international-expansion-move-b2087082.html?amp|access-date=17 April 2023|title=Hollywood Bowl buys Canadian brands in international expansion move|website=[[Independent.co.uk]] |date=25 May 2022 }} ==Brands== ===Hollywood Bowl=== A typical visit to the brand's facilities includes bowling, food, drink, amusements and pool. All of their bowling centres are equipped with at least 14 lanes, a licensed bar, Hollywood Diner and an amusements zone with a variety of games.{{cite news|url=https://www.vibe1076.co.uk/news/local-vibes-news/new-14-lane-hollywood-bowl-will-arrive-in-style-at-intu-watford/|title=New 14-lane Hollywood Bowl will arrive in style at intu Watford!|newspaper=Vibe 107.6|date=28 November 2018|access-date=6 February 2024}} ====AMF UK==== AMF Bowling was a brand that was owned by a [[AMF Bowling|USA counterpart]] which was bought by the group and has been phased out, the Worthing centre was the last UK AMF branded site and underwent a £200,000 makeover in early 2023.{{cite news|url=https://www.sussexlive.co.uk/whats-on/whats-on-news/popular-worthing-bowling-alley-undergoes-8443717|title=Popular Worthing bowling alley undergoes £200k rebranding including new VIP lanes|date=20 May 2023|newspaper=Sussex Live|access-date=6 February 2024}} ====Bowlplex==== In April 2015, the Original Bowling Company announced its intention to purchase Bowlplex, subject to approval by the Competition and Markets Authority. By late 2015, 10 Bowlplex units were acquired by the company with most of the locations being rebranded under the "Hollywood Bowl" name. With competition concerns, six Bowlplex sites were sold to [[Tenpin Ltd]] in Bristol, Camberley, Castleford, Dudley, Glasgow and Nantgarw. ===Puttstars=== Hollywood Bowl Group opened its first minigolf centre at The Springs Retail Park, [[Leeds]] in March 2020.{{cite news|url=https://www.yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk/news/people/puttstars-new-ps25m-indoor-mini-golf-experience-open-leeds-1422620|title=Puttstars - New £2.5m indoor mini golf experience to open in Leeds|date=29 July 2020|website=[[Yorkshire Evening Post]]}} ===Splitsville Bowl=== Splitsville Bowl is the brand name that is used for the company's Canadian bowling centre operations. == References == {{reflist}} == External links == * [https://www.hollywoodbowlgroup.com Group website] * Commercial websites: ** [https://www.hollywoodbowl.co.uk Hollywood Bowl centres] ** [https://www.puttstars.co.uk Puttstars centres] {{FTSE 250 Index constituents}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Companies listed on the London Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Companies in the FTSE 250 Index]] [[Category:Tenpin bowling in the United Kingdom]]
extract:
Hollywood Bowl Group is a British company that runs the Hollywood Bowl branded multi lane ten-pin bowling and Puttstars brand minigolf centres in the UK, and Splitsville Bowl branded ten-pin centres in Canada (with three centres also offering five-pin bowling, as of April 2026). 
It is listed on the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 250 Index.
